A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JAEGER and SpatialSceneQA research. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and comparable; the original appendix material is retained and relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated localization, visual grounding, reasoning, and ablation results in Tables 2–5.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds real-world transfer, architectural comparisons, and harder reasoning results in Tables 6–9.

M1.justification: The primary JAEGER architecture and Neural IV procedure remain unchanged. Appendix C introduces a limited architectural adaptation for comparison: JAEGER (BAT) replaces the FOA spatial branch with BAT Spatial-AST binaural embeddings while retaining the Qwen audio features.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on real STARSS23 recordings, restricted to approximately stationary single-speaker clips, extending the previously simulated coverage. Appendix D also introduces reasoning with four to six visible candidates beyond the original two-to-three-candidate scenarios.

E2.justification: The original Table 2 comparators remain. v2 adds SimpleFuse, which receives the same RGB-D and FOA inputs, and JAEGER (BAT), a matched-pipeline binaural comparator distinct from the existing standalone BAT baseline. These introduce substantive controls for architectural and representation advantages.

E3.justification: New protocols include pretrained-versus-scratch evaluation on 753 STARSS23 clips totaling 3.84 hours, separate median elevation and azimuth errors, matched-input and matched-pipeline comparisons, and training with 160 examples per harder candidate setting. The original experiments' stated splits, metrics, and training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices A–D add substantial analyses of simulation-to-real transfer, structured fusion versus simple input concatenation, FOA versus binaural representations, and sensitivity to more visual distractors. The original cross-scenario, depth, component, and asset-diversity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Existing mean/median reporting and the discussion of varying asset-generation seeds are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises overlap DoA errors from 16.09° to 6.44° for Classical IV and from 13.13° to 4.11° for Neural IV. Table 3 also changes 22.06° to 19.25° and 16.36° to 14.85°, respectively. No explanation establishes whether these are corrections or reruns. Tables 6–9 add substantial results, including Neural IV accuracies of 95.0%, 77.5%, and 72.5% with four, five, and six candidates; these use a different training setting from the original benchmark.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and their mathematical constructions are unchanged. The coordinate-system definitions move from Appendix B to Appendix E without substantive revision; no new theorem, proof, or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The introduction strengthens its specific headline overlap-localization result from 13.13° to 4.11°. The central contributions—JAEGER, SpatialSceneQA, and Neural IV—and the qualitative claims in the abstract and conclusion retain their scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations attributing benefits to structured representation and alignment, and explicitly limits FOA superiority to the studied comparison. It qualifies real-world transfer as a sanity check and contextualizes near-ceiling reasoning through harder scenarios and limited training. The rewritten Impact Statement adds concrete limitations concerning real acoustics, sensors, synchronization, and calibration.

D1.justification: The abstract changes from promising release upon acceptance to stating that code, checkpoints, and datasets are available at a specified GitHub repository; that availability was not externally verified. New appendices also document SimpleFuse's depth and waveform processing and the BAT branch substitution. Existing main-model hyperparameters and hardware details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and related-work positioning are retained. STARSS23 and BAT were already cited in v1. The Hear You Are reference gains an OpenReview address and submission metadata, without changing the referenced work or its positioning.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the Impact Statement, updates the resource sentence and publication footer, and inserts four appendix sections before the reordered original material. The main scientific narrative and method explanations remain largely verbatim.

P2.justification: v2 adds four compact appendix tables with captions. Table 4 moves between columns, and the unchanged Figure 4 moves to a separate final page. Existing illustrations and table structures are otherwise retained, with local text reflow rather than a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the architectural contribution by adding the input-matched SimpleFuse and matched-pipeline binaural comparisons missing from v1. The transfer and harder-candidate studies also expose applicability boundaries, supported by explicit qualifications absent previously. These gains address important evaluation weaknesses rather than merely increasing reported performance. The real-world study remains limited, harder-task training differs from the original benchmark, and the revised overlap scores remain unexplained, but the added controls and clearer limitations provide a substantial net improvement.
